overview: The Council approved several resolutions supporting state legislation on civil rights, transit electrification, and data disaggregation while celebrating Black History Month and Lunar New Year. They also addressed the abrupt retirement of the Consumer Advisory Commission staff and tabled a license for an auto repair shop pending legal review of zoning requirements.

items.title: Omori Pizza and Kitchen Common Victualler License
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license for Omori Pizza and Kitchen at 509A High Street.

items.title: Fire Department Donation
items.summary: Approved the acceptance of $1,210 in donations to the fire department's Agent Four funds in memory of Daniel Bates Jr.

items.title: Obie's Auto Service License Hearing
items.summary: Tabled a petition for an automotive repair and auto body license at 38 Harvard Avenue for one week to obtain a legal opinion on whether the application must be referred to the Community Development Board.

items.title: Condolences for Brian Branson
items.summary: Approved a resolution of condolence for community volunteer Brian Branson and dedicated the meeting to his memory.

items.title: Community Control Over Public Surveillance Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance requiring a public process for the deployment of surveillance technologies to the Public Health and Community Safety Subcommittee.

items.title: Safe Communities Act Resolution
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state legislation to protect the civil rights of undocumented residents by restricting law enforcement inquiries into immigration status.

items.title: Consumer Advisory Commission Retirements
items.summary: Congratulated three long-term staff members on their retirement and requested that the administration provide a plan to ensure the consumer office remains operational.

items.title: Public Transit Electrification Resolution
items.summary: Approved support for state legislation requiring the electrification of the MBTA bus fleet and commuter rail by 2035, despite concerns regarding potential impacts on city assessments.

items.title: Black History Month and Civics Education
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating Black History Month, amended to define specific threats of white supremacist ideology and request that the School Committee restore civics education focusing on local history.

items.title: Lunar New Year and Anti-Asian Hate
items.summary: Approved a resolution celebrating Lunar New Year and expressing solidarity with the Asian American community against rising hate crimes and bigotry.

items.title: Racial and Ethnic Data Disaggregation
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the administration report on the costs and benefits of breaking down broad racial data into specific ethnic categories, amended to include Middle Eastern and North African identities.

items.title: Equitable Representation Resolution
items.summary: Approved support for state House Bill 3155 to ensure equitable data representation at the Commonwealth level.

items.title: Committee Reports and Final Business
items.summary: Accepted reports on veterans affairs and council priorities, approved past minutes, and requested an administration report on heating failures at Medford High School.
